prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create exactly one complete native raster character sprite on a genuinely transparent RGBA background, for a side-view 2D fighting game. Square canvas, preferably 1254×1254; soft neutral diffuse light, restrained realistic game-asset materials. One character only, entire body and entire held weapon visible, with all helmet tips, fingers, skirt hem and blade tip comfortably inside the image. Place the whole silhouette within the middle 64% of the canvas with about 18% transparent padding all around. No background, floor, smoke, contact shadow, grid, lettering, watermark, framing or multiple views.

Character: Red Pyramid / Pyramid Head from the 2006 Silent Hill film, not the Silent Hill 2 game or the later films. Compose a calm static ready stance in true side-facing presentation directed RIGHT. Image 1 is a display of the original screen-used helmet and torso/right-arm prosthetics; use its final physical helmet details, weathered dark iron panels and rivet rows, scarred bare torso, and visibly stronger right arm as the highest-priority visual reference. The display's long leathery skirt is a later reconstruction, so use only its broad floor-length ochre-brown silhouette as costume support, not a claim of exact seams. The head is fully hidden inside the great pointed angular iron helmet. Bare scarred pale muscular torso, no breastplate, shoulder armor, tunic, straps or modern gloves. Long distressed dull tan leather-textured skirt with the complete ragged lower hem visible. Let the hem conceal the underlying footwear as in the display; do not invent large exposed game-style boots. No new injuries, wet gore, blood splashes or effects.

Image 2 is the original 2006 film Great Knife prop. Match its long rust-brown single blade, broad taper, pointed tip and integrated rectangular hooked handle. Hold exactly one such weapon in the right hand, lowered at his side and trailing diagonally down toward the LEFT behind him, in an idle pose with no target. The whole blade, tip and handle must remain visible and completely inside the padding. Do not shorten it to a sword, add a second weapon, serrations, chains, hooks on the blade or fantasy decorations. The right arm and knife should remain legible rather than merged into the skirt.

Image 3 is production design artwork by Andy Chung. Use it ONLY as secondary guidance for the helmet's right-facing triangular side silhouette and projection; do not copy its conceptual decorative wires, spikes, exposed inner mechanism, annotations or red painted marks. Final physical helmet surface in image 1 takes precedence. Keep this a readable lateral full-body game sprite with modest depth, no dramatic camera angle, no front-facing portrait, no crop and no extra scene.

references.role: Primary maker: original screen-used helmet, chest/back and right-arm prosthetics; display left arm was painted/scarred and skirt was recreated. Skirt/footwear exactness not certified.
Collector documentation claiming original 2006 screen-used Great Knife. Not independent studio authentication.
Production concept by Andy Chung, secondary silhouette construction only; concept details may differ from finished film.
